study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.answer: ABIDE multi-site structural MRI dataset (controls and autism)
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Cortical thickness data from ABIDE (20 samples across 17 sites); 569 healthy controls and 482 individuals with autism; FreeSurfer processed
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models... we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set"

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.answer: ABIDE controls used to train/test hierarchical Bayesian normative models; ABIDE autism sample used to evaluate clinical deviations
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Controls formed the normative training/test sets for hierarchical Bayesian regression of cortical thickness; autism participants from the same dataset were scored to check that models retained clinically useful information while removing site effects
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models... In a subsequent step, we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set"

dc3_number_of_healthy_control.detail: Model: cortical thickness normative model | Phase: overall | 569 HC; Model: cortical thickness normative model | Phase: train | 389 HC; Model: cortical thickness normative model | Phase: test | 166 HC
dc3_number_of_healthy_control.supporting_text: "we split the the healthy control data set into a training set (70% of data, n=389) and a test set (30% of data, n=166)... For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models"
dc3_number_of_healthy_control.location: Bayer2022.pdf.md: 3.3 Splitting the ABIDE data set / 3.1.1 ABIDE data set
